answer: On strict pre-provision-to-preferred-earnings conversion, the ordering is CBA first, Westpac second, NAB third. CBA turned 3% operating-performance growth into 4% cash-NPAT growth. Westpac’s pre-provision profit fell 3%, but net profit excluding Notable Items fell a lesser 2%. NAB uniquely converted positive underlying-profit growth of 1.3% into a 0.2% cash-earnings decline. That conversion ranking is not the same as the terminal earnings-growth ranking: CBA (+4%), NAB (-0.2%), Westpac (-2%). CBA’s lower loan impairment expense supplied the below-line lift. Westpac’s 3% revenue growth was overwhelmed by 9% expense growth, although lower credit charges cushioned the bottom line. NAB’s 2.9% revenue growth lagged 4.6% expense growth, and higher credit impairment charges erased the remaining underlying growth. These are directional, not like-for-like conversion ratios: the banks use different year-ends, starting measures and management exclusion policies, and Westpac describes its ex-Notable-Items basis only as comparable to a cash-earnings basis.

key_facts.fact: CBA's operating performance increased 3% and cash NPAT from continuing operations increased 4% in FY25.

citations.quote: The result was driven by a 3% increase in operating performance
Cash net profit after tax (“cash NPAT” or “cash profit”) from continuing operations increased $416 million or 4% on the prior year

key_facts.fact: CBA's operating income increased 5%, operating expenses increased 6%, and loan impairment expense decreased by $76 million.

citations.quote: The result was driven by a 3% increase in operating performance with a 5% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses 2
Loan impairment expense (LIE) decreased $76 million, reflecting an improving base case economic outlook and lower loss experience

key_facts.fact: Westpac's revenue increased 3%, expenses increased 9%, pre-provision profit declined 3%, and net profit excluding Notable Items declined 2%.

citations.quote: Net profit excluding Notable Items was $6,972 million, a decrease of 2%

key_facts.fact: Westpac's expenses increased 6% excluding restructuring costs, while credit impairment charges were $424 million or 5 basis points of average gross loans versus 7 basis points previously.

citations.quote: Excluding these costs, operating expenses increased 6% mainly due to higher staff costs and the step up in UNITE investment spend.
Credit impairment charges of $424 million represented 5 basis points of average gross loans compared to 7 basis points of average gross loans in the prior year.

key_facts.fact: NAB's revenue increased 2.9%, expenses increased 4.6%, underlying profit rose 1.3%, and cash earnings declined 0.2%.

citations.quote: Expenses increased by 4.6% including $130 million related to payroll review and remediation charges.
Underlying profit rose 1.3% over FY25, benefitting from good volume growth and stronger M&T income.

key_facts.fact: NAB's FY25 credit impairment charge was $833 million versus $728 million in FY24.

citations.quote: Credit impairment charge was $833 million, versus a FY24 charge of $728 million.

limitations: CBA cash NPAT, NAB cash earnings and Westpac net profit excluding Notable Items are management-defined non-statutory measures with different exclusions.
The pre-provision starting measures are not identically labelled or constructed, and the banks have different fiscal year-ends.
Westpac's FY25 net profit excluding Notable Items still includes the disclosed restructuring charge, limiting direct comparison with alternative underlying presentations.
The disclosures do not provide a standardized cross-bank conversion ratio, so no such ratio has been estimated.
